name: 蔡坦欣
objective:
本課程旨在提升學生資訊領域的英語文能力，加強學生於該領域課堂學習與未來職業所需的閱讀與口說技巧。本課程中，學生將經由研讀資訊領域相關文章以及針對相關主題的討論，增加資訊領域的字彙，並加強英語能力與溝通技巧。
This course is designed for students who are interested in improving English skills in the field of information technology. It aims to increase students’ reading fluency and improve their speaking skills needed to function and succeed in classroom settings and in future career. In this course, authentic reading texts related to information technology will be used. Students will discuss topics, such as artificial intelligence and the World Wide Web, in order to expand vocabulary and language skills.
schedule:
The following schedule may be adjusted according to students’ learning needs, actual teaching progress, class performance, and the university calendar.

Week 1: Course orientation; introduction to advanced information technology English; diagnostic reading and speaking activity.

Week 2: Lesson 1 The Smartest, Greenest Grid — Introduction to smart grids, energy consumption, and key vocabulary.

Week 3: Lesson 1 — Reading comprehension: EcoGrid EU, renewable energy, algorithms, and smart grid controllers.

Week 4: Lesson 1 — Discussion and short presentation: reducing energy consumption on campus; writing an energy-saving proposal email.

Week 5: Lesson 2 You Can’t Be Too Thin or Too Flexible — Future technologies, flexible electronics, and prediction language.

Week 6: Lesson 2 — Reading comprehension: flexible displays, RFID, thin silicon chips, wearable devices, and 3-D ICs.

Week 7: Lesson 2 — Technology forecast activity; short presentation on future smartphones, computers, or wearable devices.

Week 8: Lesson 3 The Real Story of Stuxnet — Introduction to computer viruses, malware, cybersecurity risks, and technical vocabulary.

Week 9: Midterm Exam Week — Midterm assessment based on Lessons 1–3, including reading comprehension, vocabulary/collocations, and an oral or written technology task.

Week 10: Lesson 3 — Reading comprehension: Stuxnet, zero-day exploits, industrial control systems, and cyber warfare.

Week 11: Lesson 3 — Skills assessment and career discussion: computer security specialists; cover letter writing practice.

Week 12: Lesson 4 All Aboard the Robotic Road Train — Introduction to self-driving cars, automation, and transportation technology.

Week 13: Lesson 4 — Reading comprehension: platooning, adaptive cruise control, autonomous vehicles, and legal challenges.

Week 14: Lesson 4 — Pros and cons of self-driving cars; structured debate on whether fully self-driving cars are feasible in the foreseeable future.

Week 15: Lesson 5 Wi-Fi Radio Takes a Digital Turn — Introduction to analog and digital technology; vocabulary related to wireless communication.

Week 16: Lesson 5 — Reading comprehension: digital radio, Wi-Fi transceivers, Moore’s Law radio, miniaturization, and integration.

Week 17: Lesson 5 — Discussion and writing task: explaining technological change and evaluating analog/digital systems.

Week 18: Final assessment: technology reading and vocabulary review; short oral presentation or written response based on Lessons 1–5; course reflection.
scorePolicy:
The final grade for this course consists of two major parts: instructor-based assessment, which accounts for 80% of the final grade, and the university English proficiency exam, which accounts for 20% of the final grade.

Instructor-based assessment: 80%

Attendance and participation: 16%. Students are expected to attend class regularly and participate actively in pair work, group discussion, textbook activities, BESTEP-style tasks, and speaking practice.

Vocabulary, reading, and in-class exercises: 20%. Students will complete textbook-based vocabulary exercises, reading comprehension tasks, collocation practice, and activities involving textual and visual information such as tables, charts, graphs, diagrams, or short academic texts.

Homework and preparation: 16%. Assignments may include vocabulary review, short reading responses, data description practice, writing tasks, short recordings, and preparation for discussions or presentations.

Midterm assessment: 12%. The midterm assessment will be based on the first half of the semester and may include vocabulary, reading comprehension, data description, and a short oral or written task.

Final assessment: 16%. The final assessment may include a short presentation, written response, reading task, vocabulary review, or integrated textual and visual information task. Students will be evaluated on clarity, organization, accuracy, content understanding, and appropriate use of course-related English.

University English proficiency exam: 20%

The university English proficiency exam accounts for 20% of the final grade. Students are required to follow the university’s official regulations and schedule for this exam.
materials:
Required textbook:
Electrical Engineering for College of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science, Book 2, CEF B1–B2.

This is a year-long course. This semester will cover Lessons 1–5 only. Lessons 6–10 will be reserved for the second semester.

Supplementary materials may include instructor-designed worksheets, vocabulary lists, slides, discussion questions, reading guides, assessment rubrics, and technology-related online materials.
延伸教學與資源: ● 混成學習 (Blended Learning) 課程結合實體授課與線上學習（同步視訊／非同步活動）。Combines face-to-face instruction with online learning (including synchronous video sessions or asynchronous activities).● 參與式創新教學 (Participatory & Innovative Teaching) 強調學生參與與產出，導入翻轉、PBL/專題、設計思考或遊戲化等策略。Emphasizes student engagement and outcomes by adopting strategies such as Flipped Classroom, PBL (Problem/Project- Based Learning), Design Thinking, or Gamification.● 數位教材資源應用 (Application of Digital Resources) 採用影音多媒體或具開放授權之資源（如 OCW、開放教科書）作為主要或輔助教材。Adopts multimedia or open-licensed resources (e.g., OCW, Open Textbooks) as primary or supplementary teaching materials.● 數位科技融入 (Digital Technology Integration) 運用生成式 AI、VR/AR、IoT、IRS 等新興科技輔助教學與評量。Utilizes emerging technologies such as Generative AI, VR/AR, IoT, and IRS (Interactive Response Systems) to facilitate teaching and assessment.
